geometry_priority_addendum.question: For one fixed complete smooth Ric>=0 metric on R^3 with normalized AVR v in (4/9,1), can limsup over integer k of h_k/(k+1)^2 exceed a fixed c in (1,9v/4)?

primary_sources.title: Colding-Minicozzi, Weyl type bounds for harmonic functions (1998)
primary_sources.location: Theorem 0.26; also quoted as a general Ric>=0 bound in Huang arXiv:2109.07534v1, Theorem 1.1 / lines 52-76
primary_sources.exact_scope: h_d <= C1(n) alpha d^(n-1) + C2(n) f(d^(n-1)), alpha=lim Vol(B_R)/R^n and f(t)=o(t); yields a universal fixed-manifold limsup constant proportional to AVR but no sharp coefficient ruling out c

primary_sources.title: Honda, Harmonic functions on asymptotic cones with Euclidean volume growth (2015)
primary_sources.version: Journal of the Mathematical Society of Japan 67 (2015), pp. 69-126
primary_sources.exact_scope: For every asymptotic cone, cone harmonic dimensions equal cross-section spectral counts and satisfy two-sided Weyl-order bounds with dimension-dependent constants; this is not an exact dimension count on the original manifold

primary_sources.title: Xu, Three circles theorems for harmonic functions (2016)
primary_sources.location: Theorem 3.2 and Theorem 3.4; degree spectrum defined in Section 2
primary_sources.exact_scope: Allows nonunique tangent cones under metric-cone/conic-measure hypotheses and gives three-circles growth propagation for exponents outside the union of cone degree spectra; does not give a harmonic-dimension limsup bound

primary_sources.title: Cai-Lai, Dimension of polynomial growth harmonic functions on locally conformally flat manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature (2026)
primary_sources.location: Theorem A and Introduction, lines 63-84 in HTML
primary_sources.exact_scope: Sharp integer Euclidean bound for the locally conformally flat Ric>=0 class; introduction says unrestricted comparison remains open and summarizes Donnelly's n>=5 subquadratic fixed-manifold examples and Huang's unique-cone asymptotic coefficient

primary_sources.title: Lin-Wang-Xu, Eigenvalues on spheres (2026)
primary_sources.location: Theorem 1.12 and Section 17; Theorem 17.1 restates the unique-cone Huang comparison
primary_sources.exact_scope: In dimension three with nonnegative sectional curvature and positive AVR, h_k<= (k+1)^2 for every integer k; release361 source metrics have negative radial sectional planes at arbitrarily large distances

primary_sources.title: Donnelly, Harmonic functions on manifolds of nonnegative Ricci curvature (2001)
primary_sources.location: Abstract and construction in the 5-page paper
primary_sources.exact_scope: Fixed Ric>=0 examples in every dimension n>=5 with more than n+1 subquadratic-growth harmonic functions, violating comparison for some real degree 1<d<2; not a 3D or high-integer-degree limsup result

primary_sources.title: Huang, Harmonic functions with polynomial growth on manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature (2023)
primary_sources.location: Theorem 1.6 and Corollaries 1.8-1.9 in arXiv v1; unique tangent cone required
primary_sources.exact_scope: With Ric>=0, maximal volume growth and unique tangent cone, gives sharp asymptotic coefficient 2 AVR/(n-1)!; in n=3 with normalized AVR v this is v

geometry_priority_addendum.bounded_conclusion: No located primary theorem proves or rules out the proposed single-metric limsup excess for general smooth 3D Ric>=0 metrics with nonunique tangent cones. General fixed-manifold and cone results retain dimension-only leading constants; exact results require unique tangent cone, local conformal flatness, or nonnegative sectional curvature. This is a plausible unresolved extension, not established novelty or a proof.
